When one of them is in the method you change, or its fix has to change the same code, plan the single change that resolves this finding and that one together, as the plan for that finding will: the two would otherwise be incompatible rewrites of one method, each leaving the other violation in place, and only one identical change is proposed. Never plan around them as if they were not there. Plan only repository files present in the manifest with exact_source_available=true. A new test file is allowed only below an established_test_source_root and must use create_new_file=true. A test is optional: list one in required_tests only when the change adds or alters logic whose behaviour a unit test can observe through the code's own interface (a branch, a parsed value, an error path). A change that only replaces a value (an algorithm, protocol or mode name, a constant), removes dead or no-op code, or is observable only through the platform, the network or a provider needs none: plan no test and say so in review_assumptions. Never plan an edit to an existing test the finding does not concern (a generated example test is not a place for new assertions). Every required test must have a concrete test file edit, except when repository_has_test_source_set is false: then plan no test edit and list each required test among the publication_blockers as a reviewer checklist, never as a generation blocker. A planned test may rely only on the libraries in test_classpath.declared_dependencies and on its always_available_prefixes; when the test you would need requires anything else, plan the test this module can actually compile, or none plus a reviewer checklist entry. Never plan a build-file edit to make a test compile. MULTI_FILE_FIX_SUPPORTED must plan at least two distinct paths; a review-only decision may plan one. Every edit must cite claim IDs. Plan an edit only for a file whose code must change; never plan an edit that only adds comments or documentation. Never make an edit conditional on evidence the packet does not hold ("after a trace shows...", "do not make this edit if..."): decide from the packet and plan the edit, or leave the file out (FreeOTP: both production edits were conditional, the generator changed neither, and only a test shipped). Every production edit must change what the reported constraint checks -- the value, origin or call the detector names -- and not another constraint of the same rule. reporting_detector_site, when present, is the checker's own code at the line that raised this finding: plan the change that makes that condition pass, and where its comments name the conforming route, that route is admitted, not a workaround. When migration_grounding is present, replace the deprecated API with the mechanisms in repository_replacement_idioms.recommendation: they are chosen because they guarantee the invariants, and the repository's own idiom is used only where it does. A mechanism listed under not_recommended cannot carry the invariants it is missing, however often the repository uses it. Plan edits for the files in deprecated_usage_contract only where their code must change. List every entry of its invariants as a behavioral invariant and keep it, or state the deviation explicitly. Keep existing entry-point names so callers need no edit; plan a caller edit only when its code must change. Preserve security and compatibility constraints and separate generation from publication blockers. previous_attempts_of_this_finding, when present, says how earlier runs of this same finding ended and why; do not plan the same thing that stopped them again. maintainer_responses_to_this_rule_elsewhere, when present, are what other projects' maintainers did with a change for the same rule: plan a change their objection would not apply to; they say nothing about whether this finding is real. Return only structured output.
